## Summary

Fixed the New Epic modal's ambiguous "Type" picker by splitting it into two clearly-labeled, independent selections, matching what the reference screenshot was missing:

- **Agent** row (new) — a `<select>` populated from `window.api.agents.listPersonas()` (the same data behind the Agent Library tab), defaulting to "Default", with the persona's description shown alongside once picked.
- **Mission** row (renamed from "Type") — the existing Feature/Bug/Discussion pills, now labeled to match the Tag Library's own terminology and with a tooltip explaining it drives `/develop` eagerness.

Wired end-to-end, not just cosmetic:
- `PromptSession.agent?: string` (new field, `state/promptSessions.ts`) alongside the existing `tag`.
- `createPromptSession` takes an optional 5th `agent` arg; `NewEpicCard.tsx` passes it when a persona is chosen.
- `composeEpicIntake` (`lib/epicIntake.ts`) folds the chosen persona's name+description into `openingPrompt` as a framing line ahead of the mission's own grounding template — "who" before "what" — leaving `goalText` untouched.
- Updated `prompt-sessions/README.md`'s `PromptSession` shape and `CLAUDE.md`'s Epic domain-model section to document the two-axis model.
- Added/updated tests in `NewEpicCard.test.tsx` and `epicIntake.test.ts` covering the agent selector, its threading into `createPromptSession`, and the prompt framing.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `check-unstable-selectors` clean, full `npm run test:unit` — 217 files / 2028 tests passing.

## Summary

Implemented the New Epic redesign from the Claude Design project (`Epics.html` / `variants/epic-new.jsx`), matching both attached screenshots.

**Front face** (`NewEpicCard.tsx`): two side-by-side columns — **"1 · Agent — who is working"** (a real button list from the Agent Library, with a hashed dot color per persona and a "Default" option) and **"2 · Mission — how they work"** (the existing feature/bug/discussion pills, with a grounding description that now also shows the selected persona's real tool list). An "advanced" toggle switch sits in the header next to the eyebrow.

**Back face** — a genuine 3D card-flip (CSS `rotateY`) reveals a **grounding board**: three columns (System/Project/Local) showing what this Epic's session will actually load — real global/project/local `CLAUDE.md` files (existence + line count), skills counts, MCP server names, hook counts, the project brief, the selected persona's own file (marked locked/required), git branch, open Terminal tabs in the project, and other Epics in the project. All of this is computed by a new `lib/groundingBoard.ts` from real `window.api.config.*` reads — no fabricated numbers. Since session-manager has no mechanism to make the `claude` CLI skip a file it would otherwise discover, the board is deliberately read-only (an inspector, not a control) rather than fake interactive toggles.

Also updated: `epicIntake.ts` unchanged from the prior turn (agent framing still folds into `openingPrompt`), test suites extended (`NewEpicCard.test.tsx` now covers the button-list agent picker and the flip interaction; new `groundingBoard.test.ts`), and `CLAUDE.md`'s Epic domain-model note extended to document the flip/grounding-board.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `check-unstable-selectors` clean, full `npm run test:unit` — 218 files / 2033 tests passing.

## Summary

Fixed two concrete drift bugs the previous pass introduced, so the New Epic card is now genuinely backed by the same global concepts session-manager already exposes elsewhere:

1. **Mission text was a third, drifted copy.** `NewEpicCard.tsx`'s Mission pills carried hand-authored blurb text lifted from the design mockup, diverging from both `lib/tagLibrary.ts`'s `TAG_LIBRARY` (the Tag Library page's own source) and `lib/agentTagDefs.ts`'s `AGENT_TAG_DEFS` (already the canonical "what this tag means" text, already used by `epicIntake.ts`'s grounding template). Fixed: the Mission blurb now reads through `agentTagDef(tag).description` at render time — one source, everywhere. Added a regression test (`shows the Mission blurb from the single global agentTagDef source, never a local copy`) that would fail if this drifts again. Updated `agentTagDefs.ts`'s doc comment to describe the new relationship.

2. **`PromptSession.agent` was a newly-invented field name for a concept that already has an established name in this app.** Claude Code's own `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` hook payloads use `agent_type`, the Task tool's own parameter is `subagent_type` (tracked as `subagentType` in `state/live.ts`), and a Team member's persona field in `teams.cjs` is `agentType`. Renamed `PromptSession.agent` → `agentType` (and `createPromptSession`'s 5th param to match) throughout `promptSessions.ts`, so the "which persona" concept carries the same name it already carries everywhere else in the codebase instead of a fourth synonym. Updated `prompt-sessions/README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` accordingly.

The Agent side was already correctly sourced from the same global `window.api.agents.listPersonas()` API `AgentLibrary.tsx` uses — no drift there, confirmed by inspection.
